headline: Coffee Shop Trains Adults With Disabilities for Real Jobs
meta_description: Life Unlimited nonprofit opens Latte Life, a working coffee shop where adults with disabilities train as baristas and find employment.
summary_short: A North Kansas City nonprofit has opened a working coffee shop where adults with disabilities train as baristas for four months before receiving job placement help.
body:
A North Kansas City nonprofit called Life Unlimited has opened Latte Life, a working coffee shop designed as a training ground for adults with disabilities. The model is straightforward: participants train as baristas over a four-month period while serving real customers in a functioning café.

What sets Latte Life apart is what comes after the training ends. Rather than leaving graduates to navigate the job market alone, Life Unlimited provides ongoing support to help them secure employment elsewhere. The coffee shop serves as both workplace and classroom—a place where people gain real-world experience, build confidence, and develop skills that employers value.

This approach transforms a simple café into a bridge between exclusion and opportunity. By combining hands-on training with genuine employment assistance, Life Unlimited addresses a persistent gap: many adults with disabilities want to work but face barriers in finding employers willing to hire them. Latte Life proves that the right structure—one that teaches, supports, and advocates—can open doors.
